name: Turn a few played notes into a self-sustaining shimmering pad by feeding them once into a clean stereo delay at 99% feedback with very different left/right times (about 1 s and 150 ms), so the melody dissolves into a continuous texture for the rest of the track
goal: Feedback-delay pad generator. Play a short phrase of three or four notes once into a neutral (uncoloured) stereo delay; nothing else is fed in for the rest of the track. Set feedback to the maximum safe value (99%) and set the delay times far apart: about 1 s on the left and about 150 ms on the right. The repeats keep cycling through the whole track; the original melody vanishes and is replaced by a shimmering secondary texture. Optional: use a tape-style delay instead for pitch warble, which strengthens the shimmer. Use the plain feedback control rather than cross-feed, which grows the signal quickly.

source.title: How to Create a Shimmering Pad

prerequisites: A stereo delay with independent left/right times and feedback up to 99%

inputs.name: phrase
inputs.description: 3-4 notes played once at the start

outputs.name: shimmer_pad
outputs.description: Self-sustaining texture that runs under the track

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Feedback near 100% can run away; feed the source only once and keep cross-feed at zero; put a limiter after the delay as a safety.
Matt prefers steady sounds: the tape-wow option adds pitch wobble, so keep it subtle or skip it.
Web Audio: two DelayNodes (1.0 s, 0.15 s) with GainNode feedback 0.99 and a ChannelMerger reproduce this.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Write a 3-4 note phrase and route it to a stereo delay set 100% wet on that channel (or on a send).
steps.expect: Only the source phrase feeds the delay.

steps.action: Set left delay about 1 s and right delay about 150 ms; set feedback to 99% on both sides; leave cross-feed at zero.
steps.expect: Repeats sustain indefinitely, with very different rhythms per side.

steps.action: Play the phrase once and let it run; do not feed more notes in.
steps.expect: The melody disappears into a shimmering continuous texture within a few cycles.

steps.action: Optional: swap to a tape-style delay with light wow/flutter to exaggerate shimmer.
steps.expect: More perceived shimmer through slight pitch variation.

steps.action: Add a limiter or level automation after the delay and check the level over the full track length.
steps.expect: Texture stays at a stable level without runaway build-up.

verification: Left and right delay times differ by roughly 6-7x (1 s vs 0.15 s).
After the source phrase ends, the texture continues for the length of the track without new input.
